issues.legal_issue: A writ court may not relegate a claimant to a civil suit merely because title or other facts are disputed, without examining whether a genuine dispute requiring that course exists.
material_facts: The claimant relied on a registered deed, earlier proceedings concerning an injunction against construction, and acquisition proceedings in which it had been treated as owner to support its title claim.
The State did not claim title, but argued that the claimant held the land for the benefit of the public and could not use it for construction.
A housing society claimed rights to enjoy the open space, while the municipal corporation asserted that the land had vested in it without explaining how that vesting occurred.
The High Court refused writ relief on the ground that a civil suit was an efficacious alternative remedy, without probing whether there was an actual serious dispute over ownership or title.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have dismissed the writ petition and relegated the claimant to a civil suit without satisfying itself that a serious dispute over ownership or title existed. The mere raising of disputed facts does not require a writ court to decline jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226, a High Court has jurisdiction to determine questions of fact, including disputed questions, although it may decline to do so as a matter of prudence where the dispute is unsuitable for writ adjudication. There is no absolute rule requiring parties to bring a civil suit whenever facts are disputed. The court relied on ABL International Ltd. v. Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. (2004) 3 SCC 553, which discussed Smt. Gunwant Kaur v. Municipal Committee, Bhatinda (1969) 3 SCC 769 and Century Spg. & Mfg. Co. Ltd. v. Ulhasnagar Municipal Council (1970) 1 SCC 582.

predicates.writ_proceeding_challenges_public_body_a: A claimant brings a writ proceeding challenging action by a public body that allegedly affects the claimant's rights.
predicates.claimant_supports_title_with_documents: The claimant relies on documentary material to support a claim of title to the property.
predicates.public_body_ownership_claim_lacks_explan: A public body asserts that the property has vested in it but does not explain the basis for that assertion.
predicates.high_court_relegates_claimant_without_ex: The High Court directs the claimant to pursue a civil suit without examining whether a serious dispute over title actually exists.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges public-body action and supports title with documents, an unexplained vesting assertion and an unexamined decision to relegate the claimant to a civil suit do not justify that relegation without a finding of a serious title dispute.

issues.legal_issue: Where land is judicially required to remain open for community use and development for public benefit is underway, the landholder's limited rights and the progress of the work may justify allowing the remaining work to be completed while preserving a claim for compensation.
material_facts: An earlier judgment had required the land to be maintained as open space for residents' access to light and air and for recreational use, and the appeal from that judgment had been dismissed.
The proposed work would develop the open space for recreational and community uses, and some of the work had been completed while the proceedings were pending.

The State contended that the claimant held the land for the benefit of residents and the public; the Court treated the landholder's use as limited to keeping the land open and stated that it could not transfer or use the land otherwise.

The Court did not determine the claimant's ultimate ownership or other entitlements and stated that any compensation claim would have to be established before an appropriate forum, including proof of title or other relevant facts where required.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were permitted to complete the remaining development work. The claimant was left to pursue any claim for compensation before the appropriate forum and would have to prove title or other relevant facts as necessary; the Court expressed no final opinion on ownership or entitlement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Pt. Chet Ram Vashist v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi (1995) 1 SCC 47: where land is earmarked and judicially required to be kept as open space for the benefit of residents and the public, the holder does not retain the ordinary attributes of ownership to transfer it or use it for another purpose and holds it for that public benefit. In determining the appropriate relief, the Court also relied on the limited rights shown by the record, the public nature of the proposed development, and the progress already made, while leaving compensation and proof of title to an appropriate forum.

rule.if: writ_appeal_challenges_development_of_claimed_land and land_is_judicially_preserved_as_open_space and landholder_is_limited_to_public_benefit_use and public_recreational_work_is_underway and some_work_has_been_completed

predicates.writ_appeal_challenges_development_of_cl: A party brings a writ appeal challenging public development work on land it claims to own.
predicates.land_is_judicially_preserved_as_open_spa: An earlier judicial decision requires the land to remain open for the benefit or enjoyment of residents or the public.
predicates.landholder_is_limited_to_public_benefit_: The landholder's use of the land is limited to maintaining it for the benefit of the community rather than transferring it or using it for another purpose.
predicates.public_recreational_work_is_underway: Public authorities are carrying out work to develop the land for recreational or other community use.
predicates.some_work_has_been_completed: A portion of the development work has been completed before the court determines the dispute.

issues.definition: If land is judicially preserved as open space, the landholder's use is limited to public benefit, and public recreational work has begun with some progress, the remaining work may be completed while a compensation claim remains available before an appropriate forum.
